Focused Neural-Behavior Validation and Artifact Screening¶

This notebook follows up on the strongest findings from the previous analysis:

  • HL17, left ventral anterior insula:

    • Ordered mean movement-related HFB: about -1.51 dB
    • Pseudorandom mean movement-related HFB: about +0.55 dB
    • Pseudorandom minus Ordered: about +2.07 dB

  • IL11, left posterior insula:

    • strongest target-direction candidate
    • circular-model R² about 0.216
    • preferred direction about 177 degrees
    • FDR q about 0.018

  • Global movement effect:

    • 198/202 contacts had negative mean HFB change
    • median channel correlation with global HFB was high
    • 120 Hz line-noise power also decreased around movement
    • many effects survived adjacent-contact bipolar rereferencing

The purpose of this notebook is not to search broadly again. It asks whether the two interesting channels still look convincing after increasingly strict checks.

Main questions¶

  1. Does HL17 still distinguish Ordered and Pseudorandom trials after:

    • removing global HFB fluctuations
    • controlling for trial number / recording drift
    • controlling for pupil size and behavioral timing
    • excluding artifact-like trials
    • bipolar rereferencing

  2. Does IL11 still show target-direction tuning after:

    • fitting the target circle more accurately
    • comparing the recorded TargetAngle with X/Y geometry
    • removing global HFB fluctuations
    • excluding artifact-like trials
    • bipolar rereferencing

  3. Do raw traces, spectra, line-noise measurements, or neighboring contacts suggest an obvious artifact?

This remains exploratory. A result that survives these checks is more convincing, but still requires replication and contact-level imaging localization.

3. Build the completed-trial table¶

Each completed trial is anchored on TargetHit and matched to the most recent MovementStarted onset with the same block and trial number.

In [4]:
def rising_edges(values):
    values = np.asarray(values)
    active = values > 0

    edges = np.flatnonzero(
        active[1:] & ~active[:-1]
    ) + 1

    if active.size and active[0]:
        edges = np.r_[0, edges]

    return edges.astype(int)


for needed in [
    "TaskBlock",
    "TaskTrial",
    "MovementStarted",
    "TargetHit",
]:
    if needed not in states:
        raise KeyError(
            f"Required state missing: {needed}"
        )

movement_onsets = rising_edges(
    states["MovementStarted"]
)

hit_samples = rising_edges(
    states["TargetHit"]
)

experimental_mask = np.ones(
    n_samples,
    dtype=bool,
)

if "Introduction" in states:
    experimental_mask &= (
        states["Introduction"] == 0
    )

experimental_mask &= states["TaskBlock"] > 0
experimental_mask &= states["TaskTrial"] > 0

if "PracticeTrial" in states:
    experimental_mask &= (
        states["PracticeTrial"] == 0
    )

movement_onsets = movement_onsets[
    experimental_mask[movement_onsets]
]

hit_samples = hit_samples[
    experimental_mask[hit_samples]
]

trial_rows = []

for hit in hit_samples:
    block = int(
        states["TaskBlock"][hit]
    )

    trial = int(
        states["TaskTrial"][hit]
    )

    candidates = movement_onsets[
        (movement_onsets <= hit)
        & (
            states["TaskBlock"][movement_onsets]
            == block
        )
        & (
            states["TaskTrial"][movement_onsets]
            == trial
        )
    ]

    if candidates.size == 0:
        continue

    onset = int(candidates[-1])

    same_trial = np.flatnonzero(
        (states["TaskBlock"] == block)
        & (states["TaskTrial"] == trial)
    )

    if same_trial.size == 0:
        continue

    trial_start = int(
        same_trial[0]
    )

    row = {
        "block": block,
        "trial": trial,
        "trial_start_sample": trial_start,
        "movement_onset_sample": onset,
        "target_hit_sample": int(hit),
        "trial_start_s": trial_start / fs,
        "movement_onset_s": onset / fs,
        "target_hit_s": hit / fs,
    }

    for name in [
        "TaskCondition",
        "TaskBlockType",
        "TargetAngle",
        "ReactionTimeMs",
        "MovementTimeMs",
        "TotalTimeMs",
    ]:
        if name in states:
            row[name] = states[name][hit]

    for coord in [
        "TargetX",
        "TargetY",
    ]:
        if coord in states:
            row[f"{coord}_move"] = (
                states[coord][onset]
            )

    if (
        "JoystickXpos" in states
        and "JoystickYpos" in states
    ):
        x = states["JoystickXpos"][
            onset:hit + 1
        ].astype(float)

        y = states["JoystickYpos"][
            onset:hit + 1
        ].astype(float)

        if len(x) >= 2:
            step = np.hypot(
                np.diff(x),
                np.diff(y),
            )

            row["joystick_path"] = (
                np.nansum(step)
            )

            row["joystick_peak_step"] = (
                np.nanmax(step)
            )

    trial_rows.append(row)

trials = pd.DataFrame(
    trial_rows
)

if trials.empty:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "No completed trials were matched."
    )

if "TaskCondition" in trials:
    trials["condition"] = (
        trials["TaskCondition"]
        .map({
            0: "Automatic",
            1: "Controlled",

if "TaskBlockType" in trials:
    trials["context"] = np.where(
        trials["TaskBlockType"] == 2,
        "Pseudorandom",
        "Ordered",

trials["analysis_trial_index"] = (
    np.arange(len(trials))
)

trials["analysis_time_min"] = (
    trials["movement_onset_s"]
    / 60.0
)

Part A: Recompute neural features and artifact metrics¶

The same movement-related windows are used as before:

  • baseline: -0.75 to -0.25 s from MovementStarted
  • movement: 0.00 to +0.50 s

For every trial and intracranial channel, this section calculates:

  • beta change
  • HFB change
  • 60, 120, and 180 Hz line-noise change
  • raw peak-to-peak amplitude
  • raw RMS

These extra metrics will be used to identify trials where apparent neural effects might be explained by unusually large raw signals or line noise.

In [5]:
BASELINE_WINDOW_S = (-0.75, -0.25)
MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S = (0.00, 0.50)

BANDS = {
    "beta": (13.0, 30.0),
    "hfb": (70.0, 150.0),
}

LINE_FREQS = [
    60.0,
    120.0,
    180.0,
]

LINE_HALF_WIDTH_HZ = 2.0


def spectral_density(segment, fs):
    nperseg = min(
        segment.shape[0],
        max(
            64,
            int(round(fs * 0.25)),
        ),
    )

    f, pxx = welch(
        segment,
        fs=fs,
        axis=0,
        nperseg=nperseg,
        noverlap=nperseg // 2,
        detrend="constant",
        scaling="density",
    )

    return f, pxx


def integrate_band(
    f,
    pxx,
    low,
    high,
    remove_line_noise=True,
):
    mask = (
        (f >= low)
        & (f <= high)
    )

    if remove_line_noise:
        for line_freq in LINE_FREQS:
            mask &= (
                np.abs(
                    f - line_freq
                )
                > LINE_HALF_WIDTH_HZ
            )

    if mask.sum() < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Not enough bins in {low}-{high} Hz."
        )

    return np.trapezoid(
        pxx[mask],
        f[mask],
        axis=0,
    )


def frequency_bin_power(
    f,
    pxx,
    target_frequency,
):
    index = np.argmin(
        np.abs(
            f - target_frequency
        )
    )

    return pxx[index]


band_responses = {
    name: []
    for name in BANDS
}

line_changes = {
    frequency: []
    for frequency in LINE_FREQS
}

baseline_rms = []
movement_rms = []

baseline_ptp = []
movement_ptp = []

kept_trials = []

for trial_index, row in trials.iterrows():
    onset = int(
        row["movement_onset_sample"]
    )

    b0 = onset + int(
        round(
            BASELINE_WINDOW_S[0]
            * fs
        )
    )

    b1 = onset + int(
        round(
            BASELINE_WINDOW_S[1]
            * fs
        )
    )

    m0 = onset + int(
        round(
            MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[0]
            * fs
        )
    )

    m1 = onset + int(
        round(
            MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[1]
            * fs
        )
    )

    if (
        b0 < 0
        or b1 > n_samples
        or m0 < 0
        or m1 > n_samples
    ):
        continue

    baseline = signal[
        b0:b1,
        intracranial_indices,
    ].astype(np.float64)

    movement = signal[
        m0:m1,
        intracranial_indices,
    ].astype(np.float64)

    f_b, psd_b = spectral_density(
        baseline,
        fs,
    )

    f_m, psd_m = spectral_density(
        movement,
        fs,
    )

    if not np.allclose(
        f_b,
        f_m,
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Frequency bins differ between baseline and movement."
        )

    for band_name, (
        low,
        high,
    ) in BANDS.items():
        base_power = integrate_band(
            f_b,
            psd_b,
            low,
            high,
            remove_line_noise=True,
        )

        move_power = integrate_band(
            f_m,
            psd_m,
            low,
            high,
            remove_line_noise=True,
        )

        band_responses[
            band_name
        ].append(
            10
            * np.log10(
                (
                    move_power
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
                /
                (
                    base_power
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
            )
        )

    for frequency in LINE_FREQS:
        base_line = frequency_bin_power(
            f_b,
            psd_b,
            frequency,
        )

        move_line = frequency_bin_power(
            f_m,
            psd_m,
            frequency,
        )

        line_changes[
            frequency
        ].append(
            10
            * np.log10(
                (
                    move_line
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
                /
                (
                    base_line
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
            )
        )

    baseline_rms.append(
        np.sqrt(
            np.nanmean(
                baseline ** 2,
                axis=0,
            )
        )
    )

    movement_rms.append(
        np.sqrt(
            np.nanmean(
                movement ** 2,
                axis=0,
            )
        )
    )

    baseline_ptp.append(
        np.nanmax(
            baseline,
            axis=0,
        )
        - np.nanmin(
            baseline,
            axis=0,
        )
    )

    movement_ptp.append(
        np.nanmax(
            movement,
            axis=0,
        )
        - np.nanmin(
            movement,
            axis=0,
        )
    )

    kept_trials.append(
        trial_index
    )

for name in band_responses:
    band_responses[name] = (
        np.vstack(
            band_responses[name]
        )
    )

for frequency in line_changes:
    line_changes[frequency] = (
        np.vstack(
            line_changes[frequency]
        )
    )

baseline_rms = np.vstack(
    baseline_rms
)

movement_rms = np.vstack(
    movement_rms
)

baseline_ptp = np.vstack(
    baseline_ptp
)

movement_ptp = np.vstack(
    movement_ptp
)

neural_trials = (
    trials.loc[
        kept_trials
    ]
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

hfb = band_responses["hfb"]
beta = band_responses["beta"]

global_hfb = np.nanmedian(
    hfb,
    axis=1,
)

print(f"Trials retained: {len(neural_trials)}")
print(f"HFB shape: {hfb.shape}")
print(f"Frequency resolution: {f_b[1] - f_b[0]:.2f} Hz")

Frequency resolution: 4.00 Hz

A1. Helper functions for interesting channels¶

In [6]:
def channel_position(channel_name):
    matches = np.flatnonzero(
        intracranial_names
        == channel_name
    )

    if matches.size != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Could not uniquely identify {channel_name}"
        )

    return int(matches[0])


def signal_index_for(channel_name):
    match = intracranial_channels.loc[
        intracranial_channels[
            "channel_name"
        ] == channel_name,
        "signal_index",
    ]

    if len(match) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Could not uniquely identify {channel_name}"
        )

    return int(
        match.iloc[0]
    )


HL17_POS = channel_position(
    "HL17"
)

IL11_POS = channel_position(
    "IL11"
)

HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX = signal_index_for(
    "HL17"
)

IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX = signal_index_for(
    "IL11"
)

print(
    f"HL17 signal index: {HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX}"
)

print(
    f"IL11 signal index: {IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX}"
)

Part B: Raw-trace artifact screening¶

The following plots are deliberately simple. They show the actual recorded voltage traces around movement onset before any HFB calculation.

For each interesting contact the notebook shows:

  • all trial traces lightly
  • the median trial trace
  • separate context traces when useful
  • raw peak-to-peak amplitude by trial

An effect driven by a few huge spikes, clipping, steps, or unstable baselines should be visible here.

In [7]:
RAW_WINDOW_S = (-1.0, 1.0)

raw_offsets = np.arange(
    int(round(RAW_WINDOW_S[0] * fs)),
    int(round(RAW_WINDOW_S[1] * fs)),
)

raw_times = raw_offsets / fs


def extract_raw_event_trials(
    signal_index,
):
    rows = []
    kept = []

    for trial_i, row in neural_trials.iterrows():
        onset = int(
            row["movement_onset_sample"]
        )

        indices = (
            onset
            + raw_offsets
        )

        if (
            indices[0] < 0
            or indices[-1] >= n_samples
        ):
            continue

        rows.append(
            signal[
                indices,
                signal_index,
            ].astype(np.float64)
        )

        kept.append(
            trial_i
        )

    return (
        np.vstack(rows),
        np.asarray(kept),
    )


def plot_raw_trial_overlay(
    channel_name,
    signal_index,
):
    raw_trials, kept = (
        extract_raw_event_trials(
            signal_index
        )
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(12, 6)
    )

    for trace in raw_trials:
        ax.plot(
            raw_times,
            trace,
            alpha=0.12,
            linewidth=0.6,
        )

    median_trace = np.nanmedian(
        raw_trials,
        axis=0,
    )

    ax.plot(
        raw_times,
        median_trace,
        linewidth=2,
        label="Median trial",
    )

    ax.axvline(
        0,
        linewidth=1,
    )

    ax.set_xlabel(
        "Time from MovementStarted (s)"
    )

    ax.set_ylabel(
        "Raw signal amplitude"
    )

    ax.set_title(
        f"{channel_name}: raw movement-aligned trials"
    )

    ax.legend()
    plt.show()

    return raw_trials, kept


hl17_raw_trials, hl17_raw_kept = (
    plot_raw_trial_overlay(
        "HL17",
        HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX,
    )
)

il11_raw_trials, il11_raw_kept = (
    plot_raw_trial_overlay(
        "IL11",
        IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX,
    )
)

B2. Raw amplitude and line-noise metrics for HL17 and IL11¶

These plots ask whether the trials with the strongest HFB responses are also the trials with the largest raw amplitudes or strongest 120 Hz changes.

In [9]:
def artifact_scatter_panel(
    channel_name,
    position,
):
    hfb_values = hfb[:, position]

    ptp_values = movement_ptp[
        :,
        position,
    ]

    rms_values = movement_rms[
        :,
        position,
    ]

    line120_values = line_changes[
        120.0
    ][
        :,
        position,
    ]

    metrics = {
        "Movement peak-to-peak": ptp_values,
        "Movement RMS": rms_values,
        "120 Hz change (dB)": line120_values,
    }

    for metric_name, values in metrics.items():
        valid = (
            np.isfinite(
                hfb_values
            )
            & np.isfinite(
                values
            )
        )

        stat = spearmanr(
            values[valid],
            hfb_values[valid],
        )

        print(
            f"{channel_name}: HFB vs {metric_name}: "
            f"rho={stat.statistic:.3f}, "
            f"p={stat.pvalue:.4g}"
        )

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(
            figsize=(7, 5)
        )

        ax.scatter(
            values[valid],
            hfb_values[valid],
        )

        ax.set_xlabel(
            metric_name
        )

        ax.set_ylabel(
            "Movement-related HFB change (dB)"
        )

        ax.set_title(
            f"{channel_name}: HFB vs {metric_name}"
        )

        plt.show()


artifact_scatter_panel(
    "HL17",
    HL17_POS,
)

artifact_scatter_panel(
    "IL11",
    IL11_POS,
)

B3. Detect artifact-like trials with robust thresholds¶

A trial is flagged for a channel when either:

  • movement peak-to-peak amplitude is more than 6 MAD above the channel median
  • movement RMS is more than 6 MAD above the channel median
  • absolute 120 Hz change is more than 6 MAD above the channel median

MAD means median absolute deviation.

This is not a universal artifact definition. It is a transparent sensitivity analysis that lets us ask whether the findings survive after obviously extreme trials are removed.

In [10]:
def robust_outlier_mask(
    values,
    threshold=6.0,
    absolute=False,
):
    values = np.asarray(
        values,
        dtype=float,
    )

    if absolute:
        values = np.abs(
            values
        )

    median = np.nanmedian(
        values
    )

    mad = np.nanmedian(
        np.abs(
            values - median
        )
    )

    if (
        not np.isfinite(mad)
        or mad == 0
    ):
        return np.zeros(
            len(values),
            dtype=bool,
        )

    robust_z = (
        0.6745
        * (values - median)
        / mad
    )

    return robust_z > threshold


def channel_artifact_mask(
    position,
):
    ptp_flag = robust_outlier_mask(
        movement_ptp[
            :,
            position,
        ]
    )

    rms_flag = robust_outlier_mask(
        movement_rms[
            :,
            position,
        ]
    )

    line_flag = robust_outlier_mask(
        line_changes[
            120.0
        ][
            :,
            position,
        ],
        absolute=True,
    )

    return (
        ptp_flag
        | rms_flag
        | line_flag
    )


hl17_artifact = channel_artifact_mask(
    HL17_POS
)

il11_artifact = channel_artifact_mask(
    IL11_POS
)

print(

    f"{hl17_artifact.sum()} / {len(hl17_artifact)}"
)

print(

Part C: Spectral checks for HL17 and IL11¶

These plots compare baseline and movement PSDs directly.

The goal is to distinguish a broad HFB change from a narrow electrical-noise peak or unusual spectral artifact.

In [11]:
def mean_psd_for_channel(
    signal_index,
):
    baseline_psds = []
    movement_psds = []
    frequencies = None

    for _, row in neural_trials.iterrows():
        onset = int(
            row["movement_onset_sample"]
        )

        b0 = onset + int(
            round(
                BASELINE_WINDOW_S[0]
                * fs
            )
        )

        b1 = onset + int(
            round(
                BASELINE_WINDOW_S[1]
                * fs
            )
        )

        m0 = onset + int(
            round(
                MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[0]
                * fs
            )
        )

        m1 = onset + int(
            round(
                MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[1]
                * fs
            )
        )

        baseline = signal[
            b0:b1,
            signal_index,
        ].astype(np.float64)

        movement = signal[
            m0:m1,
            signal_index,
        ].astype(np.float64)

        f_b, p_b = welch(
            baseline,
            fs=fs,
            nperseg=min(
                len(baseline),
                int(round(fs * 0.5)),
            ),
            detrend="constant",
            scaling="density",
        )

        f_m, p_m = welch(
            movement,
            fs=fs,
            nperseg=min(
                len(movement),
                int(round(fs * 0.5)),
            ),
            detrend="constant",
            scaling="density",
        )

        baseline_psds.append(
            p_b
        )

        movement_psds.append(
            p_m
        )

        frequencies = f_b

    return (
        frequencies,
        np.vstack(
            baseline_psds
        ),
        np.vstack(
            movement_psds
        ),
    )


def plot_psd_check(
    channel_name,
    signal_index,
):
    frequencies, baseline_psds, movement_psds = (
        mean_psd_for_channel(
            signal_index
        )
    )

    baseline_median = np.nanmedian(
        baseline_psds,
        axis=0,
    )

    movement_median = np.nanmedian(
        movement_psds,
        axis=0,
    )

    mask = (
        frequencies <= 250
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(11, 5)
    )

    ax.semilogy(
        frequencies[mask],
        baseline_median[mask],
        label="Baseline",
    )

    ax.semilogy(
        frequencies[mask],
        movement_median[mask],
        label="Movement",
    )

    for line_frequency in LINE_FREQS:
        ax.axvline(
            line_frequency,
            linewidth=0.8,
        )

    ax.set_xlabel(
        "Frequency (Hz)"
    )

    ax.set_ylabel(
        "PSD"
    )

    ax.set_title(
        f"{channel_name}: median baseline vs movement PSD"
    )

    ax.legend()
    plt.show()


plot_psd_check(
    "HL17",
    HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX,
)

plot_psd_check(
    "IL11",
    IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX,
)

C1. Time-frequency maps for both interesting channels¶

Each trial is baseline-normalized. The plots show the average spectral change around movement onset.

A narrow horizontal stripe at exactly 60/120/180 Hz would be more suspicious for line noise than a broad physiological-looking spectral change.

In [12]:
TF_WINDOW_S = (-1.25, 1.50)
TF_MAX_HZ = 220.0


def average_time_frequency(
    signal_index,
    trial_mask=None,
):
    all_power_db = []
    frequencies = None
    times = None

    for trial_i, row in neural_trials.iterrows():
        if (
            trial_mask is not None
            and not trial_mask[trial_i]
        ):
            continue

        onset = int(
            row["movement_onset_sample"]
        )

        start = onset + int(
            round(
                TF_WINDOW_S[0]
                * fs
            )
        )

        stop = onset + int(
            round(
                TF_WINDOW_S[1]
                * fs
            )
        )

        if (
            start < 0
            or stop > n_samples
        ):
            continue

        x = signal[
            start:stop,
            signal_index,
        ].astype(np.float64)

        x = (
            x
            - np.nanmean(x)
        )

        x = np.nan_to_num(
            x
        )

        f_tf, t_tf, z_tf = stft(
            x,
            fs=fs,
            nperseg=int(
                round(
                    0.25 * fs
                )
            ),
            noverlap=int(
                round(
                    0.20 * fs
                )
            ),
            boundary=None,
            padded=False,
        )

        t_tf = (
            t_tf
            + TF_WINDOW_S[0]
        )

        power = (
            np.abs(z_tf) ** 2
        )

        frequency_mask = (
            (f_tf >= 5)
            & (f_tf <= TF_MAX_HZ)
        )

        f_tf = f_tf[
            frequency_mask
        ]

        power = power[
            frequency_mask
        ]

        baseline_mask = (
            (t_tf >= BASELINE_WINDOW_S[0])
            & (t_tf <= BASELINE_WINDOW_S[1])
        )

        baseline_spectrum = (
            np.nanmean(
                power[
                    :,
                    baseline_mask,
                ],
                axis=1,
                keepdims=True,
            )
        )

        power_db = (
            10
            * np.log10(
                (
                    power
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
                /
                (
                    baseline_spectrum
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
            )
        )

        all_power_db.append(
            power_db
        )

        frequencies = f_tf
        times = t_tf

    return (
        frequencies,
        times,
        np.nanmean(
            np.stack(
                all_power_db
            ),
            axis=0,
        ),
    )


def plot_time_frequency(
    channel_name,
    signal_index,
    trial_mask=None,
    title_suffix="",
):
    frequencies, times, mean_power_db = (
        average_time_frequency(
            signal_index,
            trial_mask=trial_mask,
        )
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(11, 6)
    )

    mesh = ax.pcolormesh(
        times,
        frequencies,
        mean_power_db,
        shading="auto",
    )

    ax.axvline(
        0,
        linewidth=1,
    )

    ax.set_xlabel(
        "Time from MovementStarted (s)"
    )

    ax.set_ylabel(
        "Frequency (Hz)"
    )

    ax.set_title(
        f"{channel_name}: mean time-frequency change {title_suffix}"
    )

    fig.colorbar(
        mesh,
        ax=ax,
        label="Power change from baseline (dB)",
    )

    plt.show()


plot_time_frequency(
    "HL17",
    HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX,
)

plot_time_frequency(
    "IL11",
    IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX,
)

Part D: HL17 context effect under stricter controls¶

A major limitation of the Ordered vs Pseudorandom result is that the experiment is temporally structured: the Ordered trials occur earlier and the Pseudorandom trials later.

That means context is partially confounded with recording time.

This section asks whether HL17 still shows a context effect after accounting for:

  • linear trial drift
  • quadratic trial drift
  • pupil size
  • reaction time
  • movement time
  • joystick path
  • global HFB fluctuations
  • artifact-like trials

D3. Ordinary least-squares helper¶

This returns coefficients, standard errors, t statistics, and p-values without requiring an additional statistics package.

In [16]:
def ols_table(
    y,
    predictors,
):
    """
    predictors:
        dict of column_name -> 1D array
    """
    y = np.asarray(
        y,
        dtype=float,
    )

    predictor_names = list(
        predictors.keys()
    )

    predictor_arrays = [
        np.asarray(
            predictors[name],
            dtype=float,
        )
        for name in predictor_names
    ]

    valid = np.isfinite(
        y
    )

    for values in predictor_arrays:
        valid &= np.isfinite(
            values
        )

    y_valid = y[
        valid
    ]

    X = np.column_stack(
        [
            np.ones(
                valid.sum()
            )
        ]
        + [
            values[
                valid
            ]
            for values in predictor_arrays
        ]
    )

    names = [
        "Intercept"
    ] + predictor_names

    if (
        X.shape[0]
        <= X.shape[1]
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "Not enough valid observations for regression."
        )

    beta_hat, _, _, _ = (
        np.linalg.lstsq(
            X,
            y_valid,
            rcond=None,
        )
    )

    residuals = (
        y_valid
        - X @ beta_hat
    )

    dof = (
        X.shape[0]
        - X.shape[1]
    )

    sigma2 = (
        np.sum(
            residuals ** 2
        )
        / dof
    )

    xtx_inv = np.linalg.pinv(
        X.T @ X
    )

    standard_errors = np.sqrt(
        np.diag(
            sigma2 * xtx_inv
        )
    )

    t_values = (
        beta_hat
        / standard_errors
    )

    p_values = (
        2
        * t_distribution.sf(
            np.abs(
                t_values
            ),
            dof,
        )
    )

    ss_total = np.sum(
        (
            y_valid
            - np.mean(
                y_valid
            )
        ) ** 2
    )

    ss_res = np.sum(
        residuals ** 2
    )

    r2 = (
        1
        - ss_res / ss_total
        if ss_total > 0
        else np.nan
    )

    table = pd.DataFrame({
        "term": names,
        "coefficient": beta_hat,
        "std_error": standard_errors,
        "t": t_values,
        "p": p_values,
    })

    return (
        table,
        r2,
        valid,
        residuals,
    )

E1. HL17 adjacent bipolar pairs¶

Two local bipolar signals are evaluated:

  • HL17 - HL16
  • HL18 - HL17

If a context effect survives in one or both, it is less likely to be explained purely by a distant common reference.

In [20]:
def bipolar_signal(
    positive_name,
    negative_name,
):
    positive_index = signal_index_for(
        positive_name
    )

    negative_index = signal_index_for(
        negative_name
    )

    return (
        signal[
            :,
            positive_index,
        ].astype(np.float64)
        - signal[
            :,
            negative_index,
        ].astype(np.float64)
    )


def trial_hfb_for_1d_signal(
    one_d_signal,
):
    responses = []

    for _, row in neural_trials.iterrows():
        onset = int(
            row[
                "movement_onset_sample"
            ]
        )

        b0 = onset + int(
            round(
                BASELINE_WINDOW_S[0]
                * fs
            )
        )

        b1 = onset + int(
            round(
                BASELINE_WINDOW_S[1]
                * fs
            )
        )

        m0 = onset + int(
            round(
                MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[0]
                * fs
            )
        )

        m1 = onset + int(
            round(
                MOVEMENT_WINDOW_S[1]
                * fs
            )
        )

        baseline = one_d_signal[
            b0:b1
        ]

        movement = one_d_signal[
            m0:m1
        ]

        f_b, p_b = welch(
            baseline,
            fs=fs,
            nperseg=min(
                len(baseline),
                int(round(fs * 0.25)),
            ),
            noverlap=min(
                len(baseline),
                int(round(fs * 0.25)),
            ) // 2,
            detrend="constant",
            scaling="density",
        )

        f_m, p_m = welch(
            movement,
            fs=fs,
            nperseg=min(
                len(movement),
                int(round(fs * 0.25)),
            ),
            noverlap=min(
                len(movement),
                int(round(fs * 0.25)),
            ) // 2,
            detrend="constant",
            scaling="density",
        )

        base_power = integrate_band(
            f_b,
            p_b,
            70.0,
            150.0,
            remove_line_noise=True,
        )

        move_power = integrate_band(
            f_m,
            p_m,
            70.0,
            150.0,
            remove_line_noise=True,
        )

        responses.append(
            10
            * np.log10(
                (
                    move_power
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
                /
                (
                    base_power
                    + np.finfo(float).tiny
                )
            )
        )

    return np.asarray(
        responses
    )


hl17_minus_hl16 = (
    trial_hfb_for_1d_signal(
        bipolar_signal(
            "HL17",
            "HL16",
        )
    )
)

hl18_minus_hl17 = (
    trial_hfb_for_1d_signal(
        bipolar_signal(
            "HL18",
            "HL17",
        )
    )
)

for pair_name, values in {
    "HL17-HL16": hl17_minus_hl16,
    "HL18-HL17": hl18_minus_hl17,
}.items():
    difference = (
        np.nanmean(
            values[
                pseudo_mask
            ]
        )
        - np.nanmean(
            values[
                ordered_mask
            ]
        )
    )

    test = ttest_ind(
        values[
            pseudo_mask
        ],
        values[
            ordered_mask
        ],
        equal_var=False,
        nan_policy="omit",
    )

    print(
        f"{pair_name}: "
        f"Pseudorandom - Ordered = "
        f"{difference:.3f} dB, "
        f"p={test.pvalue:.6g}"
    )

Part F: Refine IL11 target-direction tuning¶

The target coordinates form a circle, but using the median X and Y as the center can bias the estimated angle when target sampling is uneven.

This notebook instead fits the circle center directly from the target coordinates.

In [21]:
target_x = neural_trials[
    "TargetX_move"
].astype(float).to_numpy()

target_y = neural_trials[
    "TargetY_move"
].astype(float).to_numpy()


def fit_circle_center(
    x,
    y,
):
    """
    Algebraic least-squares circle fit:
        x^2 + y^2 + D*x + E*y + F = 0
    """
    x = np.asarray(
        x,
        dtype=float,
    )

    y = np.asarray(
        y,
        dtype=float,
    )

    valid = (
        np.isfinite(x)
        & np.isfinite(y)
    )

    x = x[
        valid
    ]

    y = y[
        valid
    ]

    A = np.column_stack([
        x,
        y,
        np.ones(
            len(x)
        ),
    ])

    b = -(
        x ** 2
        + y ** 2
    )

    D, E, F = np.linalg.lstsq(
        A,
        b,
        rcond=None,
    )[0]

    center_x = -D / 2
    center_y = -E / 2

    radius = np.sqrt(
        max(
            0,
            center_x ** 2
            + center_y ** 2
            - F,
        )
    )

    return (
        center_x,
        center_y,
        radius,
    )


circle_x, circle_y, circle_radius = (
    fit_circle_center(
        target_x,
        target_y,
    )
)

dx = (
    target_x
    - circle_x
)

dy = (
    target_y
    - circle_y
)

derived_angle = (
    np.degrees(
        np.arctan2(
            -dy,
            dx,
        )
    )
    % 360
)

neural_trials[
    "target_direction_circle_deg"
] = derived_angle

print(
    f"Fitted center: "
    f"X={circle_x:.2f}, "
    f"Y={circle_y:.2f}"
)

print(
    f"Fitted radius: "
    f"{circle_radius:.2f}"
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(7, 7)
)

ax.scatter(

)

ax.scatter(

ax.plot(

F1. Compare recorded TargetAngle with X/Y-derived direction¶

TargetAngle appears to be stored in tenths of a degree. This check determines whether it is consistent with the geometry after allowing for coordinate-system orientation and offset.

In [22]:
if "TargetAngle" in neural_trials.columns:
    recorded_angle = (
        neural_trials[
            "TargetAngle"
        ].astype(float).to_numpy()
        / 10.0
    )

    # Compare both possible orientation conventions.
    candidate_1 = (
        derived_angle
    )

    candidate_2 = (
        (-derived_angle)
        % 360
    )

    def circular_offset_error(
        source,
        target,
    ):
        delta = np.deg2rad(
            (
                target
                - source
            )
            % 360
        )

        mean_vector = np.nanmean(
            np.exp(
                1j * delta
            )
        )

        offset = (
            np.degrees(
                np.angle(
                    mean_vector
                )
            )
            % 360
        )

        aligned = (
            source
            + offset
        ) % 360

        error = np.abs(
            (
                aligned
                - target
                + 180
            )
            % 360
            - 180
        )

        return (
            offset,
            np.nanmedian(
                error
            ),
            aligned,
        )

    result_1 = circular_offset_error(
        candidate_1,
        recorded_angle,
    )

    result_2 = circular_offset_error(
        candidate_2,
        recorded_angle,
    )

    if result_1[1] <= result_2[1]:
        chosen_orientation = (
            "derived"
        )
        target_angle_aligned = (
            result_1[2]
        )
        target_angle_offset = (
            result_1[0]
        )
        median_angle_error = (
            result_1[1]
        )
    else:
        chosen_orientation = (
            "reversed"
        )
        target_angle_aligned = (
            result_2[2]
        )
        target_angle_offset = (
            result_2[0]
        )
        median_angle_error = (
            result_2[1]
        )

    print(
        f"Best orientation: "
        f"{chosen_orientation}"
    )

    print(
        f"Best circular offset: "
        f"{target_angle_offset:.2f} degrees"
    )

    print(
        f"Median absolute circular error: "
        f"{median_angle_error:.2f} degrees"
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(7, 6)
    )

    ax.scatter(
        recorded_angle,
        target_angle_aligned,
    )

    ax.plot(
        [0, 360],
        [0, 360],
        linewidth=1,
    )

    ax.set_xlim(
        0,
        360,
    )

    ax.set_ylim(
        0,
        360,
    )

    ax.set_xlabel(
        "Recorded TargetAngle / 10 (degrees)"
    )

    ax.set_ylabel(
        "Aligned X/Y-derived angle (degrees)"
    )

    ax.set_title(
        "Recorded TargetAngle vs geometric target direction"
    )

    plt.show()

F2. Circular tuning helper¶

In [23]:
def circular_direction_test(
    y,
    theta_deg,
    extra_predictors=None,
):
    y = np.asarray(
        y,
        dtype=float,
    )

    theta_deg = np.asarray(
        theta_deg,
        dtype=float,
    )

    theta = np.deg2rad(
        theta_deg
    )

    predictor_columns = [
        np.cos(theta),
        np.sin(theta),
    ]

    predictor_names = [
        "cos_theta",
        "sin_theta",
    ]

    if extra_predictors is not None:
        for name, values in extra_predictors.items():
            predictor_names.append(
                name
            )

            predictor_columns.append(
                np.asarray(
                    values,
                    dtype=float,
                )
            )

    valid = np.isfinite(
        y
    )

    for values in predictor_columns:
        valid &= np.isfinite(
            values
        )

    y_valid = y[
        valid
    ]

    predictor_columns = [
        values[
            valid
        ]
        for values in predictor_columns
    ]

    X_full = np.column_stack(
        [
            np.ones(
                len(y_valid)
            )
        ]
        + predictor_columns
    )

    beta_full, _, _, _ = (
        np.linalg.lstsq(
            X_full,
            y_valid,
            rcond=None,
        )
    )

    predicted_full = (
        X_full @ beta_full
    )

    ss_full = np.sum(
        (
            y_valid
            - predicted_full
        ) ** 2
    )

    if extra_predictors is None:
        X_reduced = np.ones(
            (
                len(y_valid),
                1,
            )
        )
    else:
        extra_arrays = [
            np.asarray(
                extra_predictors[name],
                dtype=float,
            )[
                valid
            ]
            for name in extra_predictors
        ]

        X_reduced = np.column_stack(
            [
                np.ones(
                    len(y_valid)
                )
            ]
            + extra_arrays
        )

    beta_reduced, _, _, _ = (
        np.linalg.lstsq(
            X_reduced,
            y_valid,
            rcond=None,
        )
    )

    predicted_reduced = (
        X_reduced
        @ beta_reduced
    )

    ss_reduced = np.sum(
        (
            y_valid
            - predicted_reduced
        ) ** 2
    )

    df_added = 2
    df_resid = (
        len(y_valid)
        - X_full.shape[1]
    )

    if (
        df_resid <= 0
        or ss_full <= 0
    ):
        return {
            "F": np.nan,
            "p": np.nan,
            "r2": np.nan,
            "preferred_direction_deg": np.nan,
        }

    F_value = (
        (
            ss_reduced
            - ss_full
        )
        / df_added
    ) / (
        ss_full
        / df_resid
    )

    p_value = f_distribution.sf(
        F_value,
        df_added,
        df_resid,
    )

    ss_total = np.sum(
        (
            y_valid
            - np.mean(
                y_valid
            )
        ) ** 2
    )

    r2 = (
        1
        - ss_full / ss_total
        if ss_total > 0
        else np.nan
    )

    preferred_direction = (
        np.degrees(
            np.arctan2(
                beta_full[2],
                beta_full[1],
            )
        )
        % 360
    )

    return {
        "F": F_value,
        "p": p_value,
        "r2": r2,
        "preferred_direction_deg": preferred_direction,
    }

The same IL11 response is tested four ways:

  1. raw HFB
  2. after subtracting each trial's global median HFB
  3. after excluding artifact-like IL11 trials
  4. after both global-HFB removal and artifact exclusion

        "n_trials": int(

    })

F5. Permutation test for IL11 direction tuning¶

The target angles are randomly shuffled across trials while the IL11 HFB values remain fixed.

This produces an empirical null distribution for the directional F statistic.

The number of permutations can be increased for a more precise estimate.

In [26]:
N_PERMUTATIONS = 5000

observed = circular_direction_test(
    il11_hfb[
        il11_clean
    ],
    theta[
        il11_clean
    ],
)

null_f = []

clean_theta = theta[
    il11_clean
]

clean_hfb = il11_hfb[
    il11_clean
]

for _ in range(
    N_PERMUTATIONS
):
    shuffled_theta = RNG.permutation(
        clean_theta
    )

    result = circular_direction_test(
        clean_hfb,
        shuffled_theta,
    )

    null_f.append(
        result["F"]
    )

null_f = np.asarray(
    null_f
)

empirical_p = (
    1
    + np.sum(
        null_f
        >= observed["F"]
    )
) / (
    N_PERMUTATIONS
    + 1
)

print(
    f"Observed F: {observed['F']:.3f}"
)

print(
    f"Parametric p: {observed['p']:.6g}"
)

print(
    f"Permutation p: {empirical_p:.6g}"
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(8, 5)
)

ax.hist(
    null_f[
        np.isfinite(
            null_f
        )
    ],
    bins=40,
)

ax.axvline(
    observed["F"],
    linewidth=2,
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "F statistic under shuffled target directions"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Permutation count"
)

ax.set_title(
    "IL11 directional tuning permutation test"
)

Part H: Plot individual suspicious and representative trials¶

The most extreme raw-amplitude trials and strongest HFB trials are plotted for each interesting channel.

This is useful for visually checking whether the statistical relationships are driven by:

  • a single spike
  • amplifier clipping
  • a DC step
  • a burst of line noise
  • a movement artifact
In [29]:
def plot_selected_raw_trials(
    channel_name,
    signal_index,
    position,
    n_each=4,
):
    raw_trials, kept = (
        extract_raw_event_trials(
            signal_index
        )
    )

    hfb_values = hfb[
        kept,
        position,
    ]

    ptp_values = movement_ptp[
        kept,
        position,
    ]

    strongest_hfb = np.argsort(
        hfb_values
    )[
        -n_each:
    ]

    weakest_hfb = np.argsort(
        hfb_values
    )[
        :n_each
    ]

    largest_ptp = np.argsort(
        ptp_values
    )[
        -n_each:
    ]

    selected = np.unique(
        np.r_[
            strongest_hfb,
            weakest_hfb,
            largest_ptp,
        ]
    )

    for local_index in selected:
        trial_row = neural_trials.iloc[
            kept[
                local_index
            ]
        ]

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(
            figsize=(11, 4)
        )

        ax.plot(
            raw_times,
            raw_trials[
                local_index
            ],
            linewidth=0.8,
        )

        ax.axvline(
            0,
            linewidth=1,
        )

        ax.set_xlabel(
            "Time from MovementStarted (s)"
        )

        ax.set_ylabel(
            "Raw signal amplitude"
        )

        ax.set_title(
            f"{channel_name} | trial {int(trial_row['trial'])} | "
            f"{trial_row['context']} | "
            f"HFB={hfb_values[local_index]:.2f} dB | "
            f"PTP={ptp_values[local_index]:.1f}"
        )

        plt.show()


plot_selected_raw_trials(
    "HL17",
    HL17_SIGNAL_INDEX,
    HL17_POS,
)

plot_selected_raw_trials(
    "IL11",
    IL11_SIGNAL_INDEX,
    IL11_POS,
)

Part I: Final evidence table¶

This cell summarizes the main robustness checks.

Interpretation should emphasize consistency across analyses rather than any one p-value.

How to interpret this notebook¶

HL17 becomes more convincing if:¶

  • raw movement-aligned traces do not show obvious spikes or clipping
  • HFB does not strongly correlate with raw peak-to-peak or 120 Hz change
  • the context coefficient remains significant after trial drift and global HFB are included
  • the effect survives artifact-trial exclusion
  • at least one adjacent bipolar pair preserves the context effect
  • the effect is spatially localized around HL17 rather than equally large across the whole HL shaft

IL11 becomes more convincing if:¶

  • the fitted target circle agrees with TargetAngle
  • the direction effect survives global-HFB correction
  • the direction effect survives artifact-trial exclusion
  • the permutation test remains significant
  • the effect remains after context and recording drift are controlled
  • at least one adjacent bipolar pair shows similar directional tuning
  • the effect is spatially strongest around IL11 rather than uniform across the IL shaft

Reasons to be cautious¶

  • strong correlation between HFB and raw amplitude or 120 Hz changes
  • obvious transient spikes or clipping on the selected raw trials
  • disappearance after bipolar rereferencing
  • a smooth drift across the recording that mimics the context switch
  • nearly identical effects across an entire electrode shaft
  • failure of the target-angle geometry check

The strongest evidence would be a result that is temporally aligned to behavior, spatially local, reference-resistant, artifact-resistant, and replicated across recordings or participants.
